# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.

# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.

# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size. Each arm
# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 163 float32 = 1.30 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

CKPT=/data/results/mtx/mtx-l162mass-s4/net_epoch-79_state.pt

# For the mtx arms this is net_epoch-79_state.pt -- the LAST epoch --
# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.
[ -f "${CKPT}" ] || { echo "FATAL: no ${CKPT}. Run unfinished?"; ls -la /data/results/mtx/mtx-l162mass-s4 | head -20; exit 1; }

# on 2026-08-27, so a re-extraction now reads DIFFERENT jets than the
# ones under .../features -- which are what probe-bvc-v1 and the
# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py
# np.save()s unconditionally, so reusing the path would overwrite those
# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result
# already in experiments/RUNS.csv. Different sample, different path.
# The path encodes the CHECKPOINT, not just the sample. features_v2
# was written from net_best_epoch_state.pt; item 18 then made epoch 79
# the paper checkpoint, and both would have landed in the same
# directory with nothing in the cache recording which model made it.
# That is exactly how the zero-fill control came to compare epoch-79
# masked features against a best-epoch baseline. Different checkpoint,
# different path -- and extract_features.py now also refuses to write
# into a directory whose manifest names a different checkpoint.
OUT=/data/results/eval/mtx-l162mass-s4/features_e79

# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.

# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size. Each arm
# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 163 float32 = 1.30 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

CKPT=/data/results/mtx/mtx-l162mass-s5/net_epoch-79_state.pt
# CHECKPOINT RULE (DECISIONS_PENDING item 18, decided 2026-09-07).
# For the mtx arms this is net_epoch-79_state.pt -- the LAST epoch --
# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.
[ -f "${CKPT}" ] || { echo "FATAL: no ${CKPT}. Run unfinished?"; ls -la /data/results/mtx/mtx-l162mass-s5 | head -20; exit 1; }

# on 2026-08-27, so a re-extraction now reads DIFFERENT jets than the
# ones under .../features -- which are what probe-bvc-v1 and the
# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py
# np.save()s unconditionally, so reusing the path would overwrite those
# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result
# already in experiments/RUNS.csv. Different sample, different path.
# The path encodes the CHECKPOINT, not just the sample. features_v2
# was written from net_best_epoch_state.pt; item 18 then made epoch 79
# the paper checkpoint, and both would have landed in the same
# directory with nothing in the cache recording which model made it.
# That is exactly how the zero-fill control came to compare epoch-79
# masked features against a best-epoch baseline. Different checkpoint,
# different path -- and extract_features.py now also refuses to write
# into a directory whose manifest names a different checkpoint.
OUT=/data/results/eval/mtx-l162mass-s5/features_e79
mkdir -p ${OUT}

# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),

# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py

# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result
# already in experiments/RUNS.csv. Different sample, different path.

# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.

# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size. Each arm
# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 18 float32 = 0.14 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

CKPT=/data/results/mtx/mtx-r16q1mass-s4/net_epoch-79_state.pt

# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.

# ones under .../features -- which are what probe-bvc-v1 and the
# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py
# np.save()s unconditionally, so reusing the path would overwrite those
# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result

# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.

# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size. Each arm
# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 18 float32 = 0.14 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

CKPT=/data/results/mtx/mtx-r16q1mass-s5/net_epoch-79_state.pt
# CHECKPOINT RULE (DECISIONS_PENDING item 18, decided 2026-09-07).
# For the mtx arms this is net_epoch-79_state.pt -- the LAST epoch --
# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.
[ -f "${CKPT}" ] || { echo "FATAL: no ${CKPT}. Run unfinished?"; ls -la /data/results/mtx/mtx-r16q1mass-s5 | head -20; exit 1; }

# features_v2, NOT features. The file list was interleaved by family
# on 2026-08-27, so a re-extraction now reads DIFFERENT jets than the
# ones under .../features -- which are what probe-bvc-v1 and the
# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py
# np.save()s unconditionally, so reusing the path would overwrite those
# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result
# already in experiments/RUNS.csv. Different sample, different path.
# The path encodes the CHECKPOINT, not just the sample. features_v2
# was written from net_best_epoch_state.pt; item 18 then made epoch 79
# the paper checkpoint, and both would have landed in the same
# directory with nothing in the cache recording which model made it.
# That is exactly how the zero-fill control came to compare epoch-79
# masked features against a best-epoch baseline. Different checkpoint,
# different path -- and extract_features.py now also refuses to write
# into a directory whose manifest names a different checkpoint.
OUT=/data/results/eval/mtx-r16q1mass-s5/features_e79
mkdir -p ${OUT}

# same code, and a job that queues for days cannot pick up a later
# commit when it finally starts.

  https://github.com/raunavm/transferlearningsophon.git \
  /workspace/transferlearningsophon

git rev-parse HEAD
pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1

SUB2=/data/finetune/jc2

ROOT_OUT=/data/results/ft/w2b

# The subsets come from two CPU jobs applied BEFORE this one, which is
# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }
wait_for ${SUB2}/DONE
wait_for ${SUB1}/DONE
# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size.
FREE_G=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "free on /data: ${FREE_G}G"
[ "${FREE_G}" -ge 100 ] || { echo "FATAL: ${FREE_G}G free on /data, need 100G"; exit 1; }

# Every fine-tune writes up to ~4 GB (weaver keeps state + optimizer per
# epoch; leg 1 adds 2M x (128 + 162) float32 features + logits): ~250 GB
# over the wave. CLAUDE.md: no write > 1 GB past 85% without the PI.
space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

    for N in 1000 10000 100000 1000000; do
      OUT=${ROOT_OUT}/leg1/${name}/N${N}/s${S}
      [ -f ${OUT}/DONE ] && { echo "skip ${OUT} (DONE)"; continue; }
      # ONE CELL, ONE POD. mkdir creates the directory or fails, atomically,
      # so two pods can never both believe they hold a cell, whatever the
      # init lists say. A lock left by an evicted pod of THIS job is
      # re-entered (its half-written cell is moved to .partial below, as
      # always); a lock held by any OTHER job is left alone and counted.
      mkdir -p ${OUT%/*}
      if ! mkdir ${OUT}.lock 2>/dev/null; then
        owner=$(cat ${OUT}.lock/owner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "${owner}" != "${SHARD}" ]; then
          echo "LOCKED: ${OUT} is held by ${owner}, this is ${SHARD}; leaving it"
          NLOCKED=$((NLOCKED+1)); continue
        fi
        echo "re-entering ${OUT}.lock, left by an earlier pod of ${SHARD}"
      fi
      echo "${SHARD}" > ${OUT}.lock/owner
      space_ok
      attempt_ok ${OUT}
      [ -d ${OUT} ] && mv ${OUT} ${OUT}.partial.$(date -u +%s)
      mkdir -p ${OUT}
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then LOAD="--load-model-weights ${ckpt} --exclude-model-weights mod\.fc\..*"; LR=1e-4; MULT=("${HEAD_MULT[@]}"); else LOAD=""; LR=5e-4; MULT=(); fi

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
# Per shard: wave 2 and the other shards write to this same tree,
# and one job's deterministic failure must not halt another's restarts.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED.${SHARD}
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

  for S in ${seeds//,/ }; do
    for N in 1000 10000 100000 1000000; do
      OUT=${ROOT_OUT}/leg1/${name}/N${N}/s${S}
      [ -f ${OUT}/DONE ] && { echo "skip ${OUT} (DONE)"; continue; }
      # ONE CELL, ONE POD. mkdir creates the directory or fails, atomically,
      # so two pods can never both believe they hold a cell, whatever the
      # init lists say. A lock left by an evicted pod of THIS job is
      # re-entered (its half-written cell is moved to .partial below, as
      # always); a lock held by any OTHER job is left alone and counted.
      mkdir -p ${OUT%/*}
      if ! mkdir ${OUT}.lock 2>/dev/null; then
        owner=$(cat ${OUT}.lock/owner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "${owner}" != "${SHARD}" ]; then
          echo "LOCKED: ${OUT} is held by ${owner}, this is ${SHARD}; leaving it"
          NLOCKED=$((NLOCKED+1)); continue
        fi
        echo "re-entering ${OUT}.lock, left by an earlier pod of ${SHARD}"
      fi
      echo "${SHARD}" > ${OUT}.lock/owner
      space_ok
      attempt_ok ${OUT}
      [ -d ${OUT} ] && mv ${OUT} ${OUT}.partial.$(date -u +%s)
      mkdir -p ${OUT}
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then LOAD="--load-model-weights ${ckpt} --exclude-model-weights mod\.fc\..*"; LR=1e-4; MULT=("${HEAD_MULT[@]}"); else LOAD=""; LR=5e-4; MULT=(); fi
      EP=$(epochs_for ${N})
      SPE=$(samples_for ${N})
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py manifest --out ${OUT}/ft_manifest.json leg=1 init=${name} checkpoint=${ckpt} n_train=${N} ft_seed=${S} lr=${LR} head_lr_mult=50 weight_decay=0.01 wave=3 epochs=${EP} subset=${SUB2}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet data_config=configs/finetune/JetClassII_L162_noweight.yaml num_classes=162 batch_size=512 steps_per_epoch=$((N/512))
      python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py --seed ${S} --lean-val-metrics \
        --data-train ${SUB2}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet --data-val ${SUB2}/val.parquet \
        --data-config configs/finetune/JetClassII_L162_noweight.yaml \
        --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mtx.py -o num_classes 162 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
        ${COMMON} ${MULT[@]+"${MULT[@]}"} --start-lr ${LR} --samples-per-epoch ${SPE} --samples-per-epoch-val 20000 --num-epochs ${EP} \
        ${LOAD} --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --log ${OUT}/train.log 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/stdout.log
      [ -z "${ckpt}" ] || python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py load-log --log ${OUT}/stdout.log
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then
        grep -q "Parameters with lr multiplied by 50" ${OUT}/stdout.log || {
          echo "FATAL: weaver did not apply the head lr multiplier; this cell"
          echo "       ran wave 1's protocol, not ParT's published recipe."; exit 1; }
      fi
      python3 experiments/EVAL/extract_features.py --checkpoint ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt --num-classes 162 --arm FT1_${name}_N${N}_s${S} \
        --data-config configs/data/JetClassII_base.yaml --data-test ${TEST2M} \
        --out ${OUT}/features_v2 --batch-size 512 --num-workers 1 --fetch-step 1 --max-jets 2000000 --stride 4 --save-logits
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py features --dir ${OUT}/features_v2 --n 500000 --k 162
      rm -f ${OUT}/features_v2/features.npy
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: no net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT};"
        echo "       refusing to prune per-epoch checkpoints."; exit 1; }
      rm -f ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_optimizer.pt
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: the prune removed net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT}."; exit 1; }
      touch ${OUT}/DONE
      rm -rf ${OUT}.lock
    done
  done

# The subsets come from two CPU jobs applied BEFORE this one, which is
# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }

FREE_G=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "free on /data: ${FREE_G}G"
[ "${FREE_G}" -ge 100 ] || { echo "FATAL: ${FREE_G}G free on /data, need 100G"; exit 1; }

# epoch; leg 1 adds 2M x (128 + 162) float32 features + logits): ~250 GB
# over the wave. CLAUDE.md: no write > 1 GB past 85% without the PI.
space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
# Per shard: wave 2 and the other shards write to this same tree,
# and one job's deterministic failure must not halt another's restarts.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED.${SHARD}
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

for spec in ${INITS}; do
  name=${spec%%:*}; rest=${spec#*:}; ckpt=${rest%%:*}; seeds=${spec##*:}
  for S in ${seeds//,/ }; do
    for N in 1000 10000 100000 1000000; do
      OUT=${ROOT_OUT}/leg1/${name}/N${N}/s${S}
      [ -f ${OUT}/DONE ] && { echo "skip ${OUT} (DONE)"; continue; }
      # ONE CELL, ONE POD. mkdir creates the directory or fails, atomically,
      # so two pods can never both believe they hold a cell, whatever the
      # init lists say. A lock left by an evicted pod of THIS job is
      # re-entered (its half-written cell is moved to .partial below, as
      # always); a lock held by any OTHER job is left alone and counted.
      mkdir -p ${OUT%/*}
      if ! mkdir ${OUT}.lock 2>/dev/null; then
        owner=$(cat ${OUT}.lock/owner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "${owner}" != "${SHARD}" ]; then
          echo "LOCKED: ${OUT} is held by ${owner}, this is ${SHARD}; leaving it"
          NLOCKED=$((NLOCKED+1)); continue
        fi
        echo "re-entering ${OUT}.lock, left by an earlier pod of ${SHARD}"
      fi
      echo "${SHARD}" > ${OUT}.lock/owner
      space_ok
      attempt_ok ${OUT}
      [ -d ${OUT} ] && mv ${OUT} ${OUT}.partial.$(date -u +%s)
      mkdir -p ${OUT}
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then LOAD="--load-model-weights ${ckpt} --exclude-model-weights mod\.fc\..*"; LR=1e-4; MULT=("${HEAD_MULT[@]}"); else LOAD=""; LR=5e-4; MULT=(); fi

      SPE=$(samples_for ${N})

      python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py --seed ${S} --lean-val-metrics \

        --data-config configs/finetune/JetClassII_L162_noweight.yaml \
        --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mtx.py -o num_classes 162 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
        ${COMMON} ${MULT[@]+"${MULT[@]}"} --start-lr ${LR} --samples-per-epoch ${SPE} --samples-per-epoch-val 20000 --num-epochs ${EP} \
        ${LOAD} --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --log ${OUT}/train.log 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/stdout.log
      [ -z "${ckpt}" ] || python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py load-log --log ${OUT}/stdout.log
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then
        grep -q "Parameters with lr multiplied by 50" ${OUT}/stdout.log || {
          echo "FATAL: weaver did not apply the head lr multiplier; this cell"
          echo "       ran wave 1's protocol, not ParT's published recipe."; exit 1; }
      fi
      python3 experiments/EVAL/extract_features.py --checkpoint ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt --num-classes 162 --arm FT1_${name}_N${N}_s${S} \
        --data-config configs/data/JetClassII_base.yaml --data-test ${TEST2M} \
        --out ${OUT}/features_v2 --batch-size 512 --num-workers 1 --fetch-step 1 --max-jets 2000000 --stride 4 --save-logits
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py features --dir ${OUT}/features_v2 --n 500000 --k 162
      rm -f ${OUT}/features_v2/features.npy
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: no net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT};"
        echo "       refusing to prune per-epoch checkpoints."; exit 1; }
      rm -f ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_optimizer.pt
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: the prune removed net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT}."; exit 1; }
      touch ${OUT}/DONE
      rm -rf ${OUT}.lock
    done
  done
done

        --data-config configs/finetune/JetClassI_sophon_noweight.yaml \

      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then
        grep -q "Parameters with lr multiplied by 50" ${OUT}/stdout.log || {
          echo "FATAL: weaver did not apply the head lr multiplier; this cell"
          echo "       ran wave 1's protocol, not ParT's published recipe."; exit 1; }
      fi
      weaver --predict --data-test ${TEST1} ${PRED} -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --predict-output ${OUT}/pred.root 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/predict.log | tail -3

      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: no net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT};"

      rm -f ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_optimizer.pt
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: the prune removed net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT}."; exit 1; }
      touch ${OUT}/DONE
      rm -rf ${OUT}.lock
    done
  done
done

# The image carries no repo. Every other job in this repo clones.
#
# --branch takes a TAG here, not the default branch. Cloning a branch
# tip means three arms launched minutes or days apart each get
# whatever the tip was AT THAT MOMENT, so the arms could run
# different code -- precisely the channel I1 and I2 exist to close,
# and nothing downstream would notice. A tag is an exact pin, and
# --depth 1 still applies to it, so the clone stays small.
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${REPO_REF}"             https://github.com/raunavm/transferlearningsophon.git             /workspace/transferlearningsophon
cd /workspace/transferlearningsophon

# weaver reads JetClass-II parquet through pyarrow, which the cu121
# image does not ship. Fail loudly rather than at first fetch.
pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1

RUN_ID=mtx-rand-d3-s3
OUT=/data/results/mtx/${RUN_ID}
mkdir -p ${OUT}
# ATTEMPT RECORDS (scripts/add_run_records.py)
ATTEMPT=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
[ -f ${OUT}/run_manifest.json ] && cp ${OUT}/run_manifest.json ${OUT}/run_manifest.${ATTEMPT}.prev.json
mkdir -p ${OUT}/tb
[ -e ./runs ] || ln -s ${OUT}/tb ./runs

# Provenance for the two things that can drift between arms launched
# at different times. pyarrow is deliberately UNPINNED -- guessing a
# version blind is a worse risk than recording the resolved one --
# so a mismatch across arms must be detectable after the fact.
git rev-parse HEAD | tee ${OUT}/repo_commit.txt
python3 -c "import pyarrow; print(pyarrow.__version__)"             | tee ${OUT}/pyarrow_version.txt

# ---- split guard -------------------------------------------------
# All three splits live in ONE directory. A bare glob would train on
# the held-out test files and bake them into the reweighting
# histograms, which is unrecoverable: the checkpoints, not just the
# numbers, would be contaminated.
#
# This counts files that ACTUALLY EXIST, not array lengths. The array
# is a brace expansion, so its length is a compile-time constant that
# can never disagree with the number asserted next to it -- the old
# form of this guard verified nothing about the PVC at all. weaver
# resolves each path with glob.glob (train.py:187, 329) and SILENTLY
# DROPS anything missing, so a partially-populated or partially-mounted
# PVC would shrink the training set with no error anywhere.

VAL_FILES=(/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0200..0249}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0860..1074}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0280..0349}.parquet)
TEST_FILES=(/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0250..0299}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{1075..1289}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0350..0419}.parquet)
n_present () { local n=0; for f in "$@"; do [ -f "$f" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; echo $n; }
N_TRAIN=$(n_present "${TRAIN_FILES[@]}")
N_VAL=$(n_present "${VAL_FILES[@]}")
N_TEST=$(n_present "${TEST_FILES[@]}")
echo "present on PVC: train=${N_TRAIN} val=${N_VAL} test=${N_TEST}"
[ "${N_TRAIN}" -eq 1340 ] || { echo "FATAL: only ${N_TRAIN} of 1340 train files present on the PVC"; exit 1; }
[ "${N_VAL}"   -eq 335 ]   || { echo "FATAL: only ${N_VAL} of 335 val files present on the PVC"; exit 1; }

# ---- reweighting sidecar -----------------------------------------
# weaver rebuilds the flat-(pT, m_SD) histograms at startup unless a
# sidecar named <config>.<md5-of-config>.auto.yaml sits next to the
# config (utils/dataset.py:401-406). --no-remake-weights ALONE does
# NOT suppress that rebuild: the gate is
#     if remake_weights or self._data_config.reweight_hists is None
# (dataset.py:420), and these configs ship reweight_hists empty. Both
# halves are required.
#
# The sidecar must come from job-mtx-makeweight-raunav, which scans
# train+val (1675 files) per the upstream Sophon recipe. A rebuild
# here would scan --data-train only (1340 files) -- test-clean either
# way, but NOT the same histograms, and not the ones
# docs/GROUND_TRUTH.md describes.
#
# The md5 is taken from the config THIS pod cloned, so a config edited
# after the make_weight pass cannot silently pick up a stale sidecar:
# the name simply is not found and the run stops here, before the GPU.
CFG=configs/arms/RAND_d3.yaml
MD5=$(md5sum ${CFG} | cut -d' ' -f1)
SIDECAR=configs/arms/RAND_d3.${MD5}.auto.yaml
SRC=/data/results/mtx/makeweight/RAND_d3.${MD5}.auto.yaml
[ -f "${SRC}" ] || { echo "FATAL: no reweighting sidecar at ${SRC}. Run job-mtx-makeweight-raunav first. If it HAS run, then configs/arms/RAND_d3.yaml changed afterwards (its md5 is in the filename) and make_weight must be re-run."; exit 1; }
cp -v "${SRC}" "${SIDECAR}"

# The reweighting actually used by this run, preserved WITH the run.
# Without this the realised histograms are unrecoverable afterwards,
# which is a docs/RECORD.md evidence gap independent of I2.
cp -v "${SIDECAR}" ${OUT}/
sha256sum "${SIDECAR}" | tee ${OUT}/reweight_sidecar.sha256

# Manifest FIRST, so a run that dies still has one (docs/RECORD.md).

  --run-id ${RUN_ID} \
  --arm RAND_d3 \
  --num-classes 17 \
  --seed 3 \
  --data-config configs/arms/RAND_d3.yaml \
  --samples-per-epoch 10240000 \
  --num-epochs 80 \
  --batch-size 512 \
  --out ${OUT}/run_manifest.json

# AUTO-RESUME + RECIPE GUARD. See scripts/add_autoresume.py for why.
# Requires BOTH the state and optimizer file for an epoch: weaver
# writes them separately, and resuming from a state file whose
# optimizer is missing only WARNS and then trains on with a fresh
# optimizer -- silent corruption of a momentum-based run.
# THE STAMP CARRIES THE ARM CONFIG'S md5, NOT JUST THE RATE.
# job-mtx-l162-s1b exists because a rate change made the guard fire.
# Item 24 changed the VOCABULARY and left lr=5e-4 epochs=80 untouched,
# so the guard would have seen a matching stamp and resumed
# mtx-rand-d1-s1's epoch-0 checkpoint -- weights trained on the
# count-matched labels. Both vocabularies are K=17, so the head shape
# matches and torch would have loaded it WITHOUT ERROR. The md5 closes
# that: any change to configs/arms/RAND_d3.yaml now invalidates the
# stamp. (MD5 is computed above, from the config this pod cloned.)
RECIPE="lr=5e-4 epochs=80 arm=${MD5}"
RESUME=""
LAST_EP=-1
for f in ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  n=$(basename "$f" | sed 's/net_epoch-\([0-9]*\)_state\.pt/\1/')
  [ -f "${OUT}/net_epoch-${n}_optimizer.pt" ] || continue
  [ "$n" -gt "$LAST_EP" ] && LAST_EP=$n
done
if [ "$LAST_EP" -ge 0 ]; then
  # The output dir is named for gate/arm/seed, NOT for the learning
  # rate, and the per-arm rate changed when G1 returned KILL. Resuming
  # across a recipe change would blend two rates in one run silently.
  if [ ! -f "${OUT}/RECIPE" ]; then
    echo "FATAL: ${OUT} has checkpoints (through epoch ${LAST_EP}) but no"
    echo "RECIPE stamp, so the rate they were trained at is unknown."
    echo "Refusing to resume. Move that directory aside to start fresh."
    exit 1
  fi
  ON_DISK=$(cat "${OUT}/RECIPE")
  if [ "${ON_DISK}" != "${RECIPE}" ]; then
    echo "FATAL: ${OUT} holds output from a DIFFERENT recipe."
    echo "   on disk : ${ON_DISK}"
    echo "   this job: ${RECIPE}"
    echo "Refusing to resume. Move that directory aside to start fresh."
    exit 1
  fi
  RESUME="--load-epoch ${LAST_EP}"
  echo "AUTO-RESUME: complete checkpoint for epoch ${LAST_EP}, recipe matches; resuming."
else
  echo "AUTO-RESUME: no complete checkpoint; starting from scratch."
fi
printf '%s' "${RECIPE}" > ${OUT}/RECIPE
echo "${ATTEMPT} pod=${POD_NAME} node=${NODE_NAME} resume=[${RESUME:-fresh}]" >> ${OUT}/attempts.log

# seed_weaver derives four independent RNG streams and REFUSES to run
# if it cannot hook weaver's model-construction boundary -- a
# silently-partial seeding is worse than none, because the run looks
# seeded and is not.
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py \
  --lean-val-metrics \
  --seed 3 \
  --data-train Res2P:/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0000..0199}.parquet Res34P:/jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0000..0859}.parquet QCD:/jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0000..0279}.parquet \
  --data-val /jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0200..0249}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0860..1074}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0280..0349}.parquet \
  --data-config configs/arms/RAND_d3.yaml \
  --no-remake-weights \
  --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mtx.py \
  -o num_classes 17 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
  --use-amp --batch-size 512 --start-lr 5e-4 \
  --num-workers 2 --fetch-by-files --fetch-step 5 \
  --samples-per-epoch 10240000 --samples-per-epoch-val 1280000 \
  --num-epochs 80 ${RESUME} --optimizer ranger \
  --model-prefix ${OUT}/net \
  --log ${OUT}/train.log \
  --tensorboard mtx_RAND_d3_s3

# NO in-pod test evaluation here. This is deliberate.
#
# weaver accumulates EVERY test score in RAM and then concatenates
# (utils/nn/tools.py: per-batch append, then np.concatenate). Over the
# 27,448,839 selected test jets that is K-dependent and large:
#     K=162  17.8 GB of scores, ~35.6 GB peak at the concatenate
#     K=43    4.7 GB                9.4 GB
#     K=17    1.9 GB                3.7 GB
# on top of a training process whose measured anon band is 35-58 GB.
# RAND_d3 would OOM at roughly day 8 -- AFTER the whole budget was spent
# and BEFORE any output guard could fire.
#
# It is also an I1 problem: failure probability would be ~8x higher
# for RAND_d3 than R16_Q1, so the arms would not face equal risk, and the
# asymmetry runs along the studied variable.
#
# E1 reached the same conclusion and evaluated from the frozen
# checkpoint in a separate job. docs/GATES.md's requirement to cache
# full ROC arrays is met by that eval job reading
# net_best_epoch_state.pt -- not by doing it inside the training pod.
# tensorboard already on the PVC: ./runs -> ${OUT}/tb

args:
set -euo pipefail
export PYTHONPATH="/kaushik-moe-vol/code/MPT:${PYTHONPATH:-}"


DATA_CONFIG="data/JetClassII/JetClassII_full.yaml"
DATA_DIR="/kaushik-moe-vol/data/JetClassII/Pythia"

FILES=(
  "${DATA_DIR}/Res2P_0200.parquet"
  "${DATA_DIR}/Res2P_0201.parquet"
  "${DATA_DIR}/Res34P_0860.parquet"
  "${DATA_DIR}/Res34P_0861.parquet"
  "${DATA_DIR}/QCD_0280.parquet"
  "${DATA_DIR}/QCD_0281.parquet"
)

get_checkpoint () {
    RUN_DIR="$1"
    IDENTITY="${RUN_DIR}/metrics/test_eval/evaluation_identity.txt"
    LOG="${RUN_DIR}/metrics/test_eval/evaluation.log"

    if [ -f "${IDENTITY}" ]; then
        CKPT="$(grep '^checkpoint=' "${IDENTITY}" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
        if [ -n "${CKPT}" ] && [ -f "${CKPT}" ]; then
            echo "${CKPT}"
            return
        fi
    fi

    CKPT="$(
      sed -n \
        's/.*Loading model \(.*net_epoch-[0-9][0-9]*_state\.pt\) for eval.*/\1/p' \
        "${LOG}" | tail -1
    )"

    if [ -z "${CKPT}" ]; then
        CKPT="$(
          sed -n \
            "s/.*('model_prefix', '\([^']*net_epoch-[0-9][0-9]*_state\.pt\)').*/\1/p" \
            "${LOG}" | tail -1
        )"
    fi

    [ -n "${CKPT}" ] && [ -f "${CKPT}" ] || {
        echo "ERROR recovering checkpoint for ${RUN_DIR}" >&2
        exit 1
    }

    echo "${CKPT}"
}

run_interp () {
    LABEL="$1"
    RUN_DIR="$2"
    AUX="$3"

    CHECKPOINT="$(get_checkpoint "${RUN_DIR}")"
    OUT="${RUN_DIR}/interpretability-final"

    rm -rf "${OUT}"
    mkdir -p "${OUT}"

    echo "${LABEL}: ${CHECKPOINT}"

    INTERP_OUTPUT_DIR="${OUT}" \
    INTERP_RUN_NAME="${LABEL}" \
    weaver \
      --predict \
      --data-test "${FILES[@]}" \
      --data-config "${DATA_CONFIG}" \
      --network-config model/MPT_interpretability_eval.py \
      --model-prefix "${CHECKPOINT}" \
      --batch-size 512 \
      --num-workers 2 \
      --fetch-step 1.0 \
      --use-amp \
      --amp-dtype bf16 \
      --gpus 0 \
      -o num_classes 188 \
      -o fc_params "[(512,0.1)]" \
      --network-option moe_num_experts 4 \
      --network-option moe_top_k 1 \
      --network-option moe_capacity_factor 4 \
      --network-option moe_aux_loss_coef "${AUX}" \
      --network-option moe_router_jitter 0.01 \
      --predict-output "${OUT}/pred.parquet" \
      2>&1 | tee "${OUT}/collection.log"

    python3 tools/analyze_routing_interpretability.py \
      --input-dir "${OUT}" \
      2>&1 | tee "${OUT}/analysis.log"
}

run_interp \
  "aux-e4-k1-cap4-a0" \
  "/kaushik-moe-vol/outputs/runs/aux-sweep/e4-k1-cap4-aux0" \
  0.0

run_interp \
  "aux-e4-k1-cap4-a005" \
  "/kaushik-moe-vol/outputs/runs/aux-sweep/e4-k1-cap4-aux005" \
  0.05

# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 163 float32 = 1.30 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard

# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

CKPT=/data/results/mtx/mtx-l162mass-s2/net_epoch-79_state.pt

# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.

# features_v2, NOT features. The file list was interleaved by family

# recorded L162-vs-R16_Q1 numbers were computed on. extract_features.py

# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result

# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 163 float32 = 1.30 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable

# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 163 float32 = 1.30 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"
[ "${USED}" -lt 85 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data is ${USED}% full, at or over the 85% line."; df -h /data; exit 1; }

# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.
# Using it would make TRAINING DURATION an uncontrolled variable
# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.

# inputs with a different sample and silently invalidate a result

# writes ~1.1 GB (2,000,000 jets x 128 float32, plus labels and
# observers; PLUS logits.npy here, 2,000,000 x 18 float32 = 0.14 GB, whose LAST column is the mass output and not a class). The FT specs have carried a guard
# like this since the legs; the extraction specs never did, and this
# wave adds fifteen of them at once to a PVC measured at 82% on
# 2026-09-15 -- roughly 34 GB of headroom before CLAUDE.md's line.
# FAILS SAFE, verified rather than hoped: --output=pcent is GNU-only
# (the image has it -- the FT specs' --output=avail guard runs here),
# but if df ever lacked it USED would be empty, `[ "" -lt 85 ]` errors
# under set -e, and the || branch exits 1. An unparseable check refuses
# the write instead of waving it through.
USED=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "PVC used: ${USED}%"

# not weaver's net_best_epoch_state.pt. weaver's best marker is the
# argmax over ~80 validation scores that each read a DIFFERENT slice
# of the validation split: per-epoch SD is 0.047-0.075 with 4-11
# epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum, so the epoch it lands on
# (78, 74, 64, 76, 58 across the five R16_Q1 seeds) is slice luck.

# across seeds. If the file is absent the run did not finish.

# same code, and a job that queues for days cannot pick up a later
# commit when it finally starts.
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${REPO_REF}" \
  https://github.com/raunavm/transferlearningsophon.git \
  /workspace/transferlearningsophon
cd /workspace/transferlearningsophon
git rev-parse HEAD
pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

SUB2=/data/finetune/jc2
SUB1=/data/finetune/jc1
ROOT_OUT=/data/results/ft/w2b
mkdir -p ${ROOT_OUT}

# The subsets come from two CPU jobs applied BEFORE this one, which is
# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }
wait_for ${SUB2}/DONE
wait_for ${SUB1}/DONE
# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size.
FREE_G=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "free on /data: ${FREE_G}G"
[ "${FREE_G}" -ge 100 ] || { echo "FATAL: ${FREE_G}G free on /data, need 100G"; exit 1; }

# Every fine-tune writes up to ~4 GB (weaver keeps state + optimizer per
# epoch; leg 1 adds 2M x (128 + 162) float32 features + logits): ~250 GB
# over the wave. CLAUDE.md: no write > 1 GB past 85% without the PI.
space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

# The released checkpoint is gitignored, so it is never in the clone, and
# it is not on the PVC. Fetch it as E0b did and pin it to E0b's sha256.

GOT=$(sha256sum "${SOPHON}" | cut -d' ' -f1)
[ "${GOT}" = "cc7c33b522e796b5bbf0aa9bb5b01361c964f4ef3acebdd9682d7519c095b824" ] || { echo "FATAL: public checkpoint sha256 ${GOT} != E0b pin cc7c33b522e796b5bbf0aa9bb5b01361c964f4ef3acebdd9682d7519c095b824"; exit 1; }

for spec in ${INITS}; do

cd /workspace/transferlearningsophon

pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

SUB1=/data/finetune/jc1

NLOCKED=0
mkdir -p ${ROOT_OUT}

# The subsets come from two CPU jobs applied BEFORE this one, which is
# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }
wait_for ${SUB2}/DONE
wait_for ${SUB1}/DONE
# CLAUDE.md: check free space before a write of this size.
FREE_G=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "free on /data: ${FREE_G}G"
[ "${FREE_G}" -ge 100 ] || { echo "FATAL: ${FREE_G}G free on /data, need 100G"; exit 1; }

# Every fine-tune writes up to ~4 GB (weaver keeps state + optimizer per
# epoch; leg 1 adds 2M x (128 + 162) float32 features + logits): ~250 GB
# over the wave. CLAUDE.md: no write > 1 GB past 85% without the PI.
space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
# Per shard: wave 2 and the other shards write to this same tree,
# and one job's deterministic failure must not halt another's restarts.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED.${SHARD}
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }

space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

args:
set -euo pipefail
# Clone the pinned TAG (not a branch): every job in this wave runs the
# same code, and a job that queues for days cannot pick up a later
# commit when it finally starts.
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${REPO_REF}" \
  https://github.com/raunavm/transferlearningsophon.git \
  /workspace/transferlearningsophon
cd /workspace/transferlearningsophon
git rev-parse HEAD
pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

SUB2=/data/finetune/jc2
SUB1=/data/finetune/jc1
ROOT_OUT=/data/results/ft/w2b
SHARD=ft-legs-w3-c-raunav
NLOCKED=0
mkdir -p ${ROOT_OUT}

# The subsets come from two CPU jobs applied BEFORE this one, which is
# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }
wait_for ${SUB2}/DONE

space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
# Per shard: wave 2 and the other shards write to this same tree,
# and one job's deterministic failure must not halt another's restarts.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED.${SHARD}
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 2
# JetClass-I 10-class at the Sophon preprocessing: the pileup-shift leg.
TEST1=""
for C in HToBB HToCC HToGG HToWW2Q1L HToWW4Q TTBar TTBarLep WToQQ ZToQQ ZJetsToNuNu; do
  for f in $(ls /data/JetClass/Pythia/test_20M/${C}_*.root | sort | head -2); do TEST1="${TEST1} ${f}"; done
done
echo "leg-2 test subset: $(echo ${TEST1} | wc -w) files"
[ "$(echo ${TEST1} | wc -w)" -eq 20 ] || { echo "FATAL: expected 20 JetClass-I test files"; exit 1; }
PRED="--data-config configs/finetune/JetClassI_sophon_noweight.yaml --network-config experiments/E1/ParT_sophon_arch_10c.py -o num_classes 10 --predict-gpus 0 --batch-size 512 --num-workers 2 --fetch-by-files --fetch-step 1"

# The E1 arm-S reference rows (leg2/ref_e1arms-s*) are written by wave 2
# alone; they are keyed by seed, not init, and five shards racing on one
# pred.root is exactly what the per-cell lock exists to prevent.

for spec in ${INITS}; do
  name=${spec%%:*}; rest=${spec#*:}; ckpt=${rest%%:*}; seeds=${spec##*:}
  for S in ${seeds//,/ }; do
    for N in 1000 10000 100000 1000000; do
      OUT=${ROOT_OUT}/leg2/${name}/N${N}/s${S}
      [ -f ${OUT}/DONE ] && { echo "skip ${OUT} (DONE)"; continue; }
      # ONE CELL, ONE POD. mkdir creates the directory or fails, atomically,
      # so two pods can never both believe they hold a cell, whatever the
      # init lists say. A lock left by an evicted pod of THIS job is
      # re-entered (its half-written cell is moved to .partial below, as
      # always); a lock held by any OTHER job is left alone and counted.
      mkdir -p ${OUT%/*}
      if ! mkdir ${OUT}.lock 2>/dev/null; then
        owner=$(cat ${OUT}.lock/owner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "${owner}" != "${SHARD}" ]; then
          echo "LOCKED: ${OUT} is held by ${owner}, this is ${SHARD}; leaving it"
          NLOCKED=$((NLOCKED+1)); continue
        fi
        echo "re-entering ${OUT}.lock, left by an earlier pod of ${SHARD}"
      fi
      echo "${SHARD}" > ${OUT}.lock/owner
      space_ok
      attempt_ok ${OUT}
      [ -d ${OUT} ] && mv ${OUT} ${OUT}.partial.$(date -u +%s)
      mkdir -p ${OUT}
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then LOAD="--load-model-weights ${ckpt} --exclude-model-weights mod\.fc\..*"; LR=1e-4; MULT=("${HEAD_MULT[@]}"); else LOAD=""; LR=5e-4; MULT=(); fi
      EP=$(epochs_for ${N})
      SPE=$(samples_for ${N})
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py manifest --out ${OUT}/ft_manifest.json leg=2 init=${name} checkpoint=${ckpt} n_train=${N} ft_seed=${S} lr=${LR} head_lr_mult=50 weight_decay=0.01 wave=3 epochs=${EP} subset=${SUB1}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet data_config=configs/finetune/JetClassI_sophon_noweight.yaml num_classes=10 batch_size=512 steps_per_epoch=$((N/512))
      python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py --seed ${S} --lean-val-metrics \
        --data-train ${SUB1}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet --data-val ${SUB1}/val.parquet \
        --data-config configs/finetune/JetClassI_sophon_noweight.yaml \
        --network-config experiments/E1/ParT_sophon_arch_10c.py -o num_classes 10 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
        ${COMMON} ${MULT[@]+"${MULT[@]}"} --start-lr ${LR} --samples-per-epoch ${SPE} --samples-per-epoch-val 20000 --num-epochs ${EP} \
        ${LOAD} --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --log ${OUT}/train.log 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/stdout.log
      [ -z "${ckpt}" ] || python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py load-log --log ${OUT}/stdout.log
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then
        grep -q "Parameters with lr multiplied by 50" ${OUT}/stdout.log || {
          echo "FATAL: weaver did not apply the head lr multiplier; this cell"
          echo "       ran wave 1's protocol, not ParT's published recipe."; exit 1; }
      fi
      weaver --predict --data-test ${TEST1} ${PRED} -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --predict-output ${OUT}/pred.root 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/predict.log | tail -3
      [ -f ${OUT}/pred.root ] || { echo "FATAL: no pred.root in ${OUT}"; exit 1; }
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: no net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT};"
        echo "       refusing to prune per-epoch checkpoints."; exit 1; }
      rm -f ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_optimizer.pt
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: the prune removed net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT}."; exit 1; }
      touch ${OUT}/DONE
      rm -rf ${OUT}.lock
    done
  done
done

# applied only once both DONE files exist; so this wait is a guard, not
# a plan. Bounded at 2 h, and it leaves a marker: with backoffLimit 50
# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }

FREE_G=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9)
echo "free on /data: ${FREE_G}G"
[ "${FREE_G}" -ge 100 ] || { echo "FATAL: ${FREE_G}G free on /data, need 100G"; exit 1; }

# Every fine-tune writes up to ~4 GB (weaver keeps state + optimizer per
# epoch; leg 1 adds 2M x (128 + 162) float32 features + logits): ~250 GB
# over the wave. CLAUDE.md: no write > 1 GB past 85% without the PI.
space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

# A fine-tune that fails deterministically (OOM, a failed check) would
# otherwise be re-run by all 50 retries, each one moving the previous
# attempt aside: 50 x hours of a held GPU and ~200 GB of .partial dirs.
# Two attempts, then the marker stops every later pod at the top.
# Per shard: wave 2 and the other shards write to this same tree,
# and one job's deterministic failure must not halt another's restarts.
FAIL_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/FAILED.${SHARD}
[ -f ${FAIL_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt failed twice: $(cat ${FAIL_MARK}). Fix it, then remove ${FAIL_MARK}"; exit 1; }
attempt_ok () { local o=$1; local n=$(ls -d ${o}.partial.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && { echo "${o} failed ${n} times" | tee ${FAIL_MARK}; exit 1; }; return 0; }

# a bare exit 1 would re-queue and hold a GPU for 2 h per retry, the
# marker makes every retry fail at once.
WAIT_MARK=${ROOT_OUT}/WAIT_TIMEOUT.${SHARD}
[ -f ${WAIT_MARK} ] && { echo "FATAL: an earlier attempt timed out: $(cat ${WAIT_MARK}). Fix the producer, then remove ${WAIT_MARK}"; exit 1; }
wait_for () { local f=$1; local t=0; until [ -f "$f" ]; do [ "$t" -ge 7200 ] && { echo "$f absent after 2 h" | tee ${WAIT_MARK}; exit 1; }; sleep 60; t=$((t+60)); done; }

space_ok () { local p=$(df --output=pcent /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); local g=$(df -BG --output=avail /data | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9); echo "/data ${p}% used, ${g}G free"; [ "$p" -lt 92 ] && [ "$g" -ge 50 ] || { echo "FATAL: /data at ${p}% used, ${g}G free: stop and ask the PI"; exit 1; }; }

for spec in ${INITS}; do
  name=${spec%%:*}; rest=${spec#*:}; ckpt=${rest%%:*}; seeds=${spec##*:}
  for S in ${seeds//,/ }; do
    for N in 1000 10000 100000 1000000; do
      OUT=${ROOT_OUT}/leg1/${name}/N${N}/s${S}
      [ -f ${OUT}/DONE ] && { echo "skip ${OUT} (DONE)"; continue; }
      # ONE CELL, ONE POD. mkdir creates the directory or fails, atomically,
      # so two pods can never both believe they hold a cell, whatever the
      # init lists say. A lock left by an evicted pod of THIS job is
      # re-entered (its half-written cell is moved to .partial below, as
      # always); a lock held by any OTHER job is left alone and counted.
      mkdir -p ${OUT%/*}
      if ! mkdir ${OUT}.lock 2>/dev/null; then
        owner=$(cat ${OUT}.lock/owner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "${owner}" != "${SHARD}" ]; then
          echo "LOCKED: ${OUT} is held by ${owner}, this is ${SHARD}; leaving it"
          NLOCKED=$((NLOCKED+1)); continue
        fi
        echo "re-entering ${OUT}.lock, left by an earlier pod of ${SHARD}"
      fi
      echo "${SHARD}" > ${OUT}.lock/owner
      space_ok
      attempt_ok ${OUT}
      [ -d ${OUT} ] && mv ${OUT} ${OUT}.partial.$(date -u +%s)
      mkdir -p ${OUT}
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then LOAD="--load-model-weights ${ckpt} --exclude-model-weights mod\.fc\..*"; LR=1e-4; MULT=("${HEAD_MULT[@]}"); else LOAD=""; LR=5e-4; MULT=(); fi
      EP=$(epochs_for ${N})
      SPE=$(samples_for ${N})
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py manifest --out ${OUT}/ft_manifest.json leg=1 init=${name} checkpoint=${ckpt} n_train=${N} ft_seed=${S} lr=${LR} head_lr_mult=50 weight_decay=0.01 wave=3 epochs=${EP} subset=${SUB2}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet data_config=configs/finetune/JetClassII_L162_noweight.yaml num_classes=162 batch_size=512 steps_per_epoch=$((N/512))
      python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py --seed ${S} --lean-val-metrics \
        --data-train ${SUB2}/train_N${N}_s${S}.parquet --data-val ${SUB2}/val.parquet \
        --data-config configs/finetune/JetClassII_L162_noweight.yaml \
        --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mtx.py -o num_classes 162 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
        ${COMMON} ${MULT[@]+"${MULT[@]}"} --start-lr ${LR} --samples-per-epoch ${SPE} --samples-per-epoch-val 20000 --num-epochs ${EP} \
        ${LOAD} --model-prefix ${OUT}/net --log ${OUT}/train.log 2>&1 | tee ${OUT}/stdout.log
      [ -z "${ckpt}" ] || python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py load-log --log ${OUT}/stdout.log
      if [ -n "${ckpt}" ]; then
        grep -q "Parameters with lr multiplied by 50" ${OUT}/stdout.log || {
          echo "FATAL: weaver did not apply the head lr multiplier; this cell"
          echo "       ran wave 1's protocol, not ParT's published recipe."; exit 1; }
      fi
      python3 experiments/EVAL/extract_features.py --checkpoint ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt --num-classes 162 --arm FT1_${name}_N${N}_s${S} \
        --data-config configs/data/JetClassII_base.yaml --data-test ${TEST2M} \
        --out ${OUT}/features_v2 --batch-size 512 --num-workers 1 --fetch-step 1 --max-jets 2000000 --stride 4 --save-logits
      python3 experiments/FT/smoke_checks.py features --dir ${OUT}/features_v2 --n 500000 --k 162
      rm -f ${OUT}/features_v2/features.npy
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: no net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT};"
        echo "       refusing to prune per-epoch checkpoints."; exit 1; }
      rm -f ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_optimizer.pt
      [ -f ${OUT}/net_best_epoch_state.pt ] || {
        echo "FATAL: the prune removed net_best_epoch_state.pt in ${OUT}."; exit 1; }
      touch ${OUT}/DONE
      rm -rf ${OUT}.lock
    done
  done
done

  --wandb-tags "${TAGS}" \

args:
set -euo pipefail

# The image carries no repo. Every other job in this repo clones.
#
# --branch takes a TAG here, not the default branch. Cloning a branch
# tip means three arms launched minutes or days apart each get
# whatever the tip was AT THAT MOMENT, so the arms could run
# different code -- precisely the channel I1 and I2 exist to close,
# and nothing downstream would notice. A tag is an exact pin, and
# --depth 1 still applies to it, so the clone stays small.
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${REPO_REF}"             https://github.com/raunavm/transferlearningsophon.git             /workspace/transferlearningsophon
cd /workspace/transferlearningsophon

# weaver reads JetClass-II parquet through pyarrow, which the cu121
# image does not ship. Fail loudly rather than at first fetch.
pip install --no-cache-dir -q pyarrow || exit 1

RUN_ID=mtx-mpm-s1
OUT=/data/results/mtx/${RUN_ID}
mkdir -p ${OUT}
# ATTEMPT RECORDS (scripts/add_run_records.py)
ATTEMPT=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
[ -f ${OUT}/run_manifest.json ] && cp ${OUT}/run_manifest.json ${OUT}/run_manifest.${ATTEMPT}.prev.json
mkdir -p ${OUT}/tb
[ -e ./runs ] || ln -s ${OUT}/tb ./runs

# Provenance for the two things that can drift between arms launched
# at different times. pyarrow is deliberately UNPINNED -- guessing a
# version blind is a worse risk than recording the resolved one --
# so a mismatch across arms must be detectable after the fact.
git rev-parse HEAD | tee ${OUT}/repo_commit.txt
python3 -c "import pyarrow; print(pyarrow.__version__)"             | tee ${OUT}/pyarrow_version.txt

# ---- split guard -------------------------------------------------
# All three splits live in ONE directory. A bare glob would train on
# the held-out test files and bake them into the reweighting
# histograms, which is unrecoverable: the checkpoints, not just the
# numbers, would be contaminated.
#
# This counts files that ACTUALLY EXIST, not array lengths. The array
# is a brace expansion, so its length is a compile-time constant that
# can never disagree with the number asserted next to it -- the old
# form of this guard verified nothing about the PVC at all. weaver
# resolves each path with glob.glob (train.py:187, 329) and SILENTLY
# DROPS anything missing, so a partially-populated or partially-mounted
# PVC would shrink the training set with no error anywhere.
TRAIN_FILES=(/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0000..0199}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0000..0859}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0000..0279}.parquet)
VAL_FILES=(/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0200..0249}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0860..1074}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0280..0349}.parquet)
TEST_FILES=(/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0250..0299}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{1075..1289}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0350..0419}.parquet)
n_present () { local n=0; for f in "$@"; do [ -f "$f" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; echo $n; }
N_TRAIN=$(n_present "${TRAIN_FILES[@]}")
N_VAL=$(n_present "${VAL_FILES[@]}")
N_TEST=$(n_present "${TEST_FILES[@]}")
echo "present on PVC: train=${N_TRAIN} val=${N_VAL} test=${N_TEST}"
[ "${N_TRAIN}" -eq 1340 ] || { echo "FATAL: only ${N_TRAIN} of 1340 train files present on the PVC"; exit 1; }
[ "${N_VAL}"   -eq 335 ]   || { echo "FATAL: only ${N_VAL} of 335 val files present on the PVC"; exit 1; }
[ "${N_TEST}"  -eq 335 ]  || { echo "FATAL: only ${N_TEST} of 335 test files present on the PVC"; exit 1; }

# ---- reweighting sidecar -----------------------------------------
# weaver rebuilds the flat-(pT, m_SD) histograms at startup unless a
# sidecar named <config>.<md5-of-config>.auto.yaml sits next to the
# config (utils/dataset.py:401-406). --no-remake-weights ALONE does
# NOT suppress that rebuild: the gate is
#     if remake_weights or self._data_config.reweight_hists is None
# (dataset.py:420), and these configs ship reweight_hists empty. Both
# halves are required.
#
# The sidecar must come from job-mtx-makeweight-raunav, which scans
# train+val (1675 files) per the upstream Sophon recipe. A rebuild
# here would scan --data-train only (1340 files) -- test-clean either
# way, but NOT the same histograms, and not the ones
# docs/GROUND_TRUTH.md describes.
#
# The md5 is taken from the config THIS pod cloned, so a config edited
# after the make_weight pass cannot silently pick up a stale sidecar:
# the name simply is not found and the run stops here, before the GPU.
CFG=configs/arms/L188.yaml
MD5=$(md5sum ${CFG} | cut -d' ' -f1)
SIDECAR=configs/arms/L188.${MD5}.auto.yaml
SRC=/data/results/mtx/makeweight/L188.${MD5}.auto.yaml
[ -f "${SRC}" ] || { echo "FATAL: no reweighting sidecar at ${SRC}. Run job-mtx-makeweight-l188-raunav first. If it HAS run, then configs/arms/L188.yaml changed afterwards (its md5 is in the filename) and make_weight must be re-run."; exit 1; }
cp -v "${SRC}" "${SIDECAR}"

# The reweighting actually used by this run, preserved WITH the run.
# Without this the realised histograms are unrecoverable afterwards,
# which is a docs/RECORD.md evidence gap independent of I2.
cp -v "${SIDECAR}" ${OUT}/
sha256sum "${SIDECAR}" | tee ${OUT}/reweight_sidecar.sha256

# Manifest FIRST, so a run that dies still has one (docs/RECORD.md).
python3 scripts/write_run_manifest.py \
  --run-id ${RUN_ID} \
  --arm MPM \
  --num-classes 0 \
  --mpm-mask-rate 0.40 \
  --seed 1 \
  --data-config configs/arms/L188.yaml \
  --samples-per-epoch 10240000 \
  --num-epochs 80 \
  --batch-size 512 \
  --out ${OUT}/run_manifest.json

# AUTO-RESUME + RECIPE GUARD. See scripts/add_autoresume.py for why.
# Requires BOTH the state and optimizer file for an epoch: weaver
# writes them separately, and resuming from a state file whose
# optimizer is missing only WARNS and then trains on with a fresh
# optimizer -- silent corruption of a momentum-based run.
RECIPE='lr=5e-4 epochs=80 mpm-mask=0.40'
RESUME=""
LAST_EP=-1
for f in ${OUT}/net_epoch-*_state.pt; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  n=$(basename "$f" | sed 's/net_epoch-\([0-9]*\)_state\.pt/\1/')
  [ -f "${OUT}/net_epoch-${n}_optimizer.pt" ] || continue
  [ "$n" -gt "$LAST_EP" ] && LAST_EP=$n
done
if [ "$LAST_EP" -ge 0 ]; then
  # The output dir is named for gate/arm/seed, NOT for the learning
  # rate, and the per-arm rate changed when G1 returned KILL. Resuming
  # across a recipe change would blend two rates in one run silently.
  if [ ! -f "${OUT}/RECIPE" ]; then
    echo "FATAL: ${OUT} has checkpoints (through epoch ${LAST_EP}) but no"
    echo "RECIPE stamp, so the rate they were trained at is unknown."
    echo "Refusing to resume. Move that directory aside to start fresh."
    exit 1
  fi
  ON_DISK=$(cat "${OUT}/RECIPE")
  if [ "${ON_DISK}" != "${RECIPE}" ]; then
    echo "FATAL: ${OUT} holds output from a DIFFERENT recipe."
    echo "   on disk : ${ON_DISK}"
    echo "   this job: ${RECIPE}"
    echo "Refusing to resume. Move that directory aside to start fresh."
    exit 1
  fi
  RESUME="--load-epoch ${LAST_EP}"
  echo "AUTO-RESUME: complete checkpoint for epoch ${LAST_EP}, recipe matches; resuming."
else
  echo "AUTO-RESUME: no complete checkpoint; starting from scratch."
fi
printf '%s' "${RECIPE}" > ${OUT}/RECIPE
echo "${ATTEMPT} pod=${POD_NAME} node=${NODE_NAME} resume=[${RESUME:-fresh}]" >> ${OUT}/attempts.log

# seed_weaver derives four independent RNG streams and REFUSES to run
# if it cannot hook weaver's model-construction boundary -- a
# silently-partial seeding is worse than none, because the run looks
# seeded and is not.
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 python3 experiments/E1/seed_weaver.py \
  --mpm --mpm-mask-rate 0.40 \
  --seed 1 \
  --data-train Res2P:/jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0000..0199}.parquet Res34P:/jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0000..0859}.parquet QCD:/jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0000..0279}.parquet \
  --data-val /jc2/jet_data/Res2P_{0200..0249}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/Res34P_{0860..1074}.parquet /jc2/jet_data/QCD_{0280..0349}.parquet \
  --data-config configs/arms/L188.yaml \
  --no-remake-weights \
  --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mpm.py \
  --use-amp --batch-size 512 --start-lr 5e-4 \
  --num-workers 2 --fetch-by-files --fetch-step 5 \
  --samples-per-epoch 10240000 --samples-per-epoch-val 1280000 \
  --num-epochs 80 ${RESUME} --optimizer ranger \
  --model-prefix ${OUT}/net \
  --log ${OUT}/train.log \
  --tensorboard mtx_MPM_s1

# NO in-pod test evaluation here. This is deliberate.
#
# weaver accumulates EVERY test score in RAM and then concatenates
# (utils/nn/tools.py: per-batch append, then np.concatenate). Over the
# 27,448,839 selected test jets that is K-dependent and large:
#     K=162  17.8 GB of scores, ~35.6 GB peak at the concatenate
#     K=43    4.7 GB                9.4 GB
#     K=17    1.9 GB                3.7 GB
# on top of a training process whose measured anon band is 35-58 GB.
# L162 would OOM at roughly day 8 -- AFTER the whole budget was spent
# and BEFORE any output guard could fire.
#
# It is also an I1 problem: failure probability would be ~8x higher
# for L162 than R16_Q1, so the arms would not face equal risk, and the
# asymmetry runs along the studied variable.
#
# E1 reached the same conclusion and evaluated from the frozen
# checkpoint in a separate job. docs/GATES.md's requirement to cache
# full ROC arrays is met by that eval job reading
# net_best_epoch_state.pt -- not by doing it inside the training pod.
# tensorboard already on the PVC: ./runs -> ${OUT}/tb
containers.name: train

# so the guard would have seen a matching stamp and resumed

  # across a recipe change would blend two rates in one run silently.

    echo "   this job: ${RECIPE}"
    echo "Refusing to resume. Move that directory aside to start fresh."

  echo "AUTO-RESUME: complete checkpoint for epoch ${LAST_EP}, recipe matches; resuming."

# seed_weaver derives four independent RNG streams and REFUSES to run
# if it cannot hook weaver's model-construction boundary -- a
# silently-partial seeding is worse than none, because the run looks
# seeded and is not.

  --lean-val-metrics \
  --seed 2 \

  --data-config configs/arms/RAND_d2.yaml \
  --no-remake-weights \
  --network-config experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mtx.py \
  -o num_classes 17 -o fc_params '[(512,0.1)]' \
  --use-amp --batch-size 512 --start-lr 5e-4 \
  --num-workers 2 --fetch-by-files --fetch-step 5 \
  --samples-per-epoch 10240000 --samples-per-epoch-val 1280000 \
  --num-epochs 80 ${RESUME} --optimizer ranger \

# and BEFORE any output guard could fire.

# for RAND_d2 than R16_Q1, so the arms would not face equal risk, and the

N_VAL=$(n_present "${VAL_FILES[@]}")
N_TEST=$(n_present "${TEST_FILES[@]}")
